title: Involute spur gear
purpose: Generate a spur gear whose tooth flanks are true involutes of the base circle, sized by module, tooth count and pressure angle, extruded around a bore. Use it for mechanisms, clocks and props.

entry_points.name: involute_function
entry_points.summary: inv(a) = tan(a) - a, the polar angle swept by the involute at pressure angle a.

entry_points.name: gear_radii
entry_points.summary: (pitch, base, addendum, root) radii: z m / 2, pitch cos(alpha), pitch + m, pitch - 1.25 m.

entry_points.name: gear_profile
entry_points.signature: gear_profile(teeth=18, module=0.1, pressure_angle=20.0, flank_samples=6, tip_samples=3, root_samples=4)
entry_points.summary: The counter-clockwise 2D outline of the gear, tooth 0 centred on +X.

entry_points.name: spur_gear
entry_points.signature: spur_gear(teeth=18, module=0.1, pressure_angle=20.0, thickness=0.25, bore_radius=0.18, flank_samples=6)
entry_points.summary: The gear extruded along Y and centred at the origin: two capped faces (triangulated around the bore) and quad side walls, closed and outward. With a bore the solid has genus 1.

entry_points.name: build
entry_points.signature: build(teeth=18, module=0.1, pressure_angle=20.0, thickness=0.25, bore_radius=0.18, flank_samples=6)
entry_points.summary: The gear the command line writes: each cap shares its vertices under one flat normal and every wall quad owns its corners, so edges between caps and walls and between flank segments stay crisp.

entry_points.name: main
entry_points.summary: Command line: write the gear as .gltf or .obj and print a JSON summary.

parameters.name: module
parameters.meaning: Pitch diameter divided by the tooth count; meshing gears share it.

parameters.name: pressure_angle
parameters.meaning: Angle between the line of action and the pitch circle tangent.

parameters.name: bore_radius
parameters.meaning: Radius of the centre hole; 0 for none. Must stay inside the root circle.

outputs.content: the gear with POSITION and NORMAL: caps share vertices under one normal, wall quads own their corners
the same gear as Wavefront OBJ

limits: Standard full-depth teeth (addendum 1 module, dedendum 1.25 modules) without profile shift, tip relief or a root fillet: the flank meets the root circle with a radial segment. No backlash is added. Gears with very few teeth undercut in reality; this outline does not model that. The volume check compares with the exact area of the smooth outline within 0.5 percent.
technique_references: Involute of a circle and the involute function inv(a) = tan a - a
Tooth thickness of half the circular pitch at the pitch circle
Ear clipping with a bridged hole for the caps
